title.narrative: Production and sale of organic vegetables in the central Altiplano of Guatemala.

description.narrative: Website Farming families in the community of San Juan Comalapa Guatemala are struggling: soil degradation and adverse weather are further squeezing their chances of profitably living off agriculture. At the IAF we are committed to community-led solutions that improve food security and expand economic opportunity through sustainable smallholder agriculture. Our grantee partner Asociacin de Productores Comalapenses (ASPROC) helps smallholder farmers meet these challenges through a combination of training technical assistance farmer-to-farmer exchanges and access to inputs and technologies to strengthen their production. With IAF support ASPROC is consolidating gains in sustainable agriculture increasing income improving quality of life and reducing the drivers of irregular migration. This grant is part of the IAF's efforts to address the root causes of irregular migration in Central America. FY22 This amendment provides ASPROC with an additional two years and $248,830 to expand its organic vegetable production and produce organic fertilizer and fungicide to increase productivity and crop yields. ASPROC will also encourage sustainable agricultural practices among more farmers. As part of the amendment, ASPROC is mobilizing an additional $364,097 in counterpart resources to the grant agreement. FY24 This amendment provides ASPROC with an additional two and a half years and $350,600 to expand its organic vegetable production, train other farmers in organic production, and form a network of organic fertilizer producers who can register and sell organic inputs. As part of the amendment, ASPROC is mobilizing an additional $525,550 in counterpart resources to the grant agreement.
